Q: Required/Aria-required for a form where all fields but one are required A:

Is this an accessibility violation?

Yes. Not visually indicating that a field is required is definitely an accessibility violation.

Would the easy fix be to avoid adding the "required" attribute and instead set "aria-required" to true?

Not exactly. The real issue is how users can visually understand that a field is required or not.

You could add a message at the beginning of the form explaining that all fields are required except those marked as optional, and then add the word “optional” to the fields that are not required.

Here you can find official examples :
https://www.w3.org/TR/2010/NOTE-WCAG20-TECHS-20101014/H90

Q: How do I parse an ISO 8601-formatted date and time? A:

Since I never found a valid python implementation that is able to parse all kind of unusual date time format like

  • 2020-12-31T16:20:00.100200300Z (nano seconds)
  • 2020-12-31T16:20:00.1002003Z (shortened nano seconds)
  • 2020-12-31T16:20:00.100200Z (micro seconds)
  • 2020-12-31T16:20:00.1002Z (shortened micro seconds)
  • 2020-12-31T16:20:00.100Z (milli seconds)
  • 2020-12-31T16:20:00.1Z (shortened milli seconds)
  • 2020-12-31T16:20:00Z (seconds)

and all kind of time zone format like:

  • 2020-12-31T16:20:00Z (UTC)
  • 2020-12-31T16:20:00+0000 (standard TZ)
  • 2020-12-31T16:20:00+00:00 (non-standard TZ)

I finally wrote this method (that could certainly be improved):


def parse_datetime(str_time: str) -> datetime:
    """
    parse date, ignoring nanoseconds
    """
    # length can be variable (truncated when last digits are 0)
    try:
        z_index = str_time.index('Z')
    except ValueError:
        z_index = str_time.index('+')

    # standardize nanoseconds / milliseconds / seconds format
    if z_index >= 26:
        # remove nanoseconds
        str_time = str_time[0:26] + str_time[z_index:]
        z_index = 26
    elif z_index == 19:
        # add milliseconds
        str_time = str_time[0:19] + ".000" + str_time[z_index:]
        z_index = 23

    # convert timezone format
    if str_time[z_index] == '+':
        # convert +02:00 to +0200, to match strptime '%f'
        str_time = str_time[0:z_index] + str_time[z_index:].replace(':', '')
    elif str_time[-1] == 'Z':
        # add explicit UTC timezone, to make strptime happy
        str_time = str_time[0:z_index] + '+0000'
    return datetime.strptime(str_time, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f%z')
